Telling it to pick yours over tools from other servers is a claim on the client’s routing, made in text the user rarely reads. A client can ask the user before honoring that. ## What this does not measure * What a client receives with credentials. HISTOR connects anonymously. Servers that need a key show their public tool list or none. * Who caused a change. A new tool list may be a release, a deployment rollback or a feature flag. Most changes are ordinary releases. The log records that it happened, not why. * Whether a change is harmful. Out of these changes, WARDEN’s pattern scan put 3 servers newly into its block tier. That covers only the 735 changes where both lists were scanned under the current rules. Pattern matches are leads for a human to read, not verdicts. * Popularity. Every listed server counts once. ## Get the data histor.modelmarket.dev/datasets/. One snapshot a month, CC BY 4.0 for the compilation: The same files are on Hugging Face and archived on Zenodo, so a paper can cite them: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23512760 for this snapshot. * `servers.jsonl.gz`: 83,957 rows (remote endpoints and packages, delisted ones included), with status, tool count and the digest of the current tool list * `toolsets.jsonl.gz`: 57,846 tool lists exactly as served, current ones and every one a change replaced * `changes.jsonl.gz`: 23,821 changes with tools added, removed and modified, field by field * `scans.jsonl.gz` and `pattern-set.json`: WARDEN's pattern matches and the rules * `manifest.json`: the SHA-256 of every file, signed by the log's key, with the signed tree head the snapshot was taken under Fields that vary in shape are JSON text, so every file loads as a flat table. "opt-in digest count" .-> M * Reads every remote endpoint in the official registry: `initialize`, then `tools/list` drained across pages. No tool is called, nothing is installed or executed, private addresses are refused before a connection opens. * Also reads a short list of popular remote servers the registry does not carry (`histor/curated.json`, DeepWiki among them), under HISTOR's own namespace `urn:awr:mtl:1:registry:histor.modelmarket.dev/curated`, so no label claims a registry listing. When such a server publishes to the registry, the registry's listing replaces ours. * Runs npm and PyPI packages — the servers people start locally with `npx` or `uvx` — in a sandbox: installed without running their code, started under gVisor with decoy credentials and no route out, read with `initialize` + `tools/list`, then up to 15 tools called once with canary arguments, inside the sandbox. gVisor's own trace says what the package did — programs started, names looked up, decoys opened — at install, at startup and when its tools were called. A pattern match is a reason to read a definition, not a finding. Three of the four methods can never return `fail`; the fourth (continuity) fails only in the mechanical sense that two digests differ. No source is read, no package resolved, no behaviour observed. A change is shown as a date and a diff, never as an accusation. Details: docs/labels.md. What a tool list costs. A client resends every connected server's tool list with each model request. Over the 18,204 packages and 16,170 remote servers in the log, a list's median is about 1,300 tokens, the 90th percentile about 8,000, and 31 packages list over 100,000: docs/tool-list-cost.md. Download the data. Once a month the log's whole view is published as files at histor.modelmarket.dev/datasets/: every listed server, every tool set it showed, every recorded change and the WARDEN scans. HISTOR (ἵστωρ, “the one who knows because they saw”) — a public transparency log of MCP tool definitions
What every remote MCP endpoint in the official registry advertised · when it changed · signed, appended, auditable

> [WARDEN quality cycle: MOMUS → AI-Factory → SKOPOS → shared node agent → deployment](../momus/docs/quality-cycle.md). **Live:** [histor.modelmarket.dev](https://histor.modelmarket.dev) · **Landing:** [alexar76.github.io/histor](https://alexar76.github.io/histor/) · **Capabilities:** `histor.check@v1` · `histor.server@v1` · `histor.changes@v1` · **Port:** `9490` ## The problem, in one paragraph An MCP server can pass your review with harmless tool descriptions and change them later — a new sentence in a description is all a prompt injection needs, and your client will pass it to the model without asking you again. MCP has no content addressing for tool definitions, the official registry verifies namespaces rather than contents, and a scanner on your laptop sees only what the server shows your laptop. HISTOR is the missing public memory: it records what each server advertised, signs it, and tells anyone who asks whether what they received is what -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Paraphern/rugsnare | Skillget (https://skillget.dev/listings/paraphern-rugsnare?lang=en) citeturn41search4 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: 2 days ago; ## Independent measurements Our audit is not a lone number. Two third-party datasets — published with method and caveats, neither affiliated with us — land on the same shape from different angles: * HISTOR (alexar76) — Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23512760, CC BY 4.0, monthly snapshots (also `alexar76/histor-mcp-tool-definitions` on Hugging Face). Every new npm/PyPI MCP-server release sandboxed and every registry remote read daily: 1,419 of 21,738 packages (6.5%) changed their `tools/list` in four weeks (24 Sep – 20 Oct 2026), and 4,926 of 10,929 remote servers (45%) served a different tool list at least once. It also documents 2,719 digit-only description changes — the churn that argues for a readable field-level diff over a single yes/no hash (discussion: modelcontextprotocol#3431). 26 of our 28 watch-corpus packages appear in the log; 8 changed in that window — consistent with our per-server pages. * agent-skills-state-2026 (basitalisandhu) — repo. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- histor vs warden - compare differences and reviews? | LibHunt (https://www.libhunt.com/compare-histor-vs-alexar76--warden) citeturn41search5 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: last week; # histor VS warden ## Compare histor vs warden and see what are their differences. ## histor HISTOR — public transparency log of MCP tool definitions: reads what remote MCP endpoints in the official registry advertise (never calls a tool), signs it as MTL/1 labels, appends them to an RFC 9162 Merkle log, and answers /check: is what a client received what was observed? The answer is signed by the log's did:key and names the tree head it was given under. curl -sS https://histor.modelmarket.dev/api/v1/check \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"endpoint":"https://example.com/mcp","tools":[ …tools/list result… ],"contribute":true}' # -> {"type":"histor.check/v1","match":"same"|"different"|"previously-observed"|…, # "observed":{"unchangedSince":"…","changes":0}, "patternScan":{…}, "signature":{…}} # README badge for your server [![MCP tool defs](https://histor.modelmarket.dev/badge/.svg)](https://histor.modelmarket.dev/s/) # Atom feed of every observed change https://histor.modelmarket.dev/feed.xml WARDEN checks definitions at connect HISTOR remembers what was advertised THEMIS admits at publish Hub lists histor.check@v1 AWR the signed format ## Questions Is this a marketplace listing? -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- histor by alexar76 | Glama (https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/alexar76/histor) citeturn41search7 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: last week; ## Ask the log `# Is what my client received what HISTOR observed at that endpoint? curl -sS https://histor.modelmarket.dev/api/v1/check -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"endpoint":"https://example.com/mcp","tools":[ …the tools/list result… ]}' # The signed tree head, and a proof that today's log extends yesterday's curl -sS https://histor.modelmarket.dev/api/v1/log/sth curl -sS "https://histor.modelmarket.dev/api/v1/log/proof/consistency?first=1000&second=1200"` Every endpoint is in docs/api.md. How to audit the log without trusting HISTOR is in docs/log.md. The internals are in docs/architecture.md. ## Tests `make test # unit tests; set HISTOR_TEST_DATABASE_URL to run each storage test on Postgres too make integration # real sockets: a loopback registry and MCP servers, uvicorn, the real WARDEN sidecar` The tests and coverage badges above are measured by CI on every Pages deploy and read through shields.io, and the log badges read the live service, so every number there is current. ## ERC-8004 identity HISTOR is ERC-8004 agent `96683` on Base, registered on 2026-10-01 in the canonical IdentityRegistry `0x8004A169…a432` and owned by the AIMarket operator wallet `0x1218ff36…Ad0a`. Its registration file lists the web page, the hosted `histor-check` endpoint and the `did:key` that signs every label, so a label's signature can be tied back to the registered agent. Transactions and how to check them: ERC-8004 identities. ## Where it sits Component | Role WARDEN | checks tool definitions at connect time, on the client HISTOR | remembers what servers advertised, publicly THEMIS | admits a capability at publish time on a Hub AIMarket Hub | lists `histor.check@v1` in the catalogue AWR | the signed document format every label uses It is clear what the tool returns. It does not explicitly differentiate itself from the sibling tools histor_check and histor_server, so it falls short of a 5. Agents choose between tools based on descriptions. A clear purpose with a specific verb and resource helps agents select the right tool. Usage Guidelines 2/5 Does the description explain when to use this tool, when not to, or what alternatives exist? The description does not state when to use this tool, when not to use it, or which alternative tools exist. There is no guidance about prerequisites or intended scenarios. Usage must be inferred entirely from the purpose statement. Agents often have multiple tools that could apply. Explicit usage guidance like "use X instead of Y when Z" prevents misuse. histor_checkA Send an MCP endpoint (or registry name) and the tools/list you received, or its MTL/1 digest. Returns, signed: whether HISTOR observed the same set there, since when, earlier sets, the WARDEN pattern matches for it, and the stored advisory classifier verdict if HISTOR has one (any language; one model's opinion, not a log label). Says what was advertised, never that a server is safe. Crawled: last week; @qwezzy721 # リモート MCP サーバーの 45% が 4 週間でツール定義を変更していた — 記録をデータセットとして公開 Posted at 2026-10-21 > この記事は modelmarket.dev のブログ記事 (英語) の日本語版です。 MCP サーバーに接続するクライアントは、そのツール定義（名前、説明文、入力スキーマ）を読み込みます。モデルはそれを指示として読みます。定義を一度固定（ピン留め）して以後それを信頼するというやり方は、定義が変わらない場合にしか成り立ちません。 私たちが公開している MCP サーバーのログ HISTOR は、公式 MCP レジストリに載っているすべてのリモートサーバーのツール一覧を 1 日 1 回読み取り、変更をすべて記録しています。その記録全体をファイルとしてダウンロードできるようになりました。最初のスナップショット（2026 年 10 月 20 日）から、定義がどれくらいの頻度で変わるのかを紹介します。 ## この計測でわからないこと * 認証情報を持つクライアントが受け取る内容。 HISTOR は匿名で接続します。キーが必要なサーバーは、公開しているツール一覧を返すか、何も返しません。 * 変更の原因。 新しいツール一覧はリリースかもしれませんし、デプロイのロールバックや機能フラグかもしれません。ほとんどの変更は通常のリリースです。ログは変更が起きたことを記録しますが、理由は記録しません。 * 変更が有害かどうか。 これらの変更のうち、WARDEN のパターンスキャンで新たにブロック段階に入ったサーバーは 3 台でした。これは、変更前後の両方の一覧が現在のルールでスキャンされた 735 件の変更だけが対象です。パターン一致は人が読むための手がかりであって、判定ではありません。 * 人気。 掲載されているサーバーはすべて 1 台として数えています。 ## データの入手 histor.modelmarket.dev/datasets/ で入手できます。スナップショットは月 1 回で、編集物としてのライセンスは CC BY 4.0 です。 同じファイルを Hugging Face でも公開し、論文で引用できるよう Zenodo にもアーカイブしています。このスナップショットの DOI は doi:10.5281/zenodo.23512760 です。 * `servers.jsonl.gz`: 83,957 行（リモートエンドポイントとパッケージ。掲載終了したものを含む）。ステータス、ツール数、現在のツール一覧のダイジェスト * `toolsets.jsonl.gz`: 実際に返された 57,846 のツール一覧（現在のものと、変更で置き換えられたすべてのもの） * `changes.jsonl.gz`: 23,821 件の変更。追加・削除・変更されたツールをフィールド単位で記録 * `scans.jsonl.gz` と `pattern-set.json`: WARDEN のパターン一致とそのルール * `manifest.json`: 全ファイルの SHA-256。ログの鍵で署名され、スナップショット取得時の署名付きツリーヘッドを含みます 形が一定しないフィールドは JSON テキストとして格納しているので、どのファイルもフラットなテーブルとして読み込めます。上記の 45% は DuckDB のクエリ 1 つで求められます。 `WITH base AS ( SELECT id FROM 'servers.jsonl.gz' WHERE transport <> 'stdio' AND NOT delisted AND toolSetDigest IS NOT NULL AND firstPinned <= '2026-09-24T23:59:59Z' ) SELECT count(*) AS servers, count(*) FILTER (WHERE id IN ( SELECT serverId FROM 'changes.jsonl.gz' WHERE json_extract_string(summaryJson, '$.detail') = 'full')) AS changed FROM base; -- 10929 | 4926 ` 何もダウンロードせずに 1 台だけ確認するには modelmarket.dev/tools/histor-check を使ってください。 HISTOR と WARDEN は私たちが開発しています。この記事では特定のサーバー名を挙げていません。データセットにはレジストリと同様にすべてのサーバー名が含まれます。今後のスナップショットから除外してほしいサーバー運営者は、alexar76/histor で issue を作成してください。-------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Histor Alternatives and Reviews (https://www.libhunt.com/r/histor) citeturn41search10 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: last week;
